catalogue.name: finmesh-typology-catalogue
catalogue.source: AMLworld laundering patterns (Altman et al., NeurIPS 2023). Descriptions are written for this project; no text is copied from FATF or FinCEN documents.

review.pass_2: owner, before any X6 result (see docs/protocol/attribution_mapping.md)

stages.placement: Illicit cash or funds first enter the financial system.
stages.layering: Funds are moved through transfers and accounts to hide where they came from.
stages.integration: Funds return to the launderer as apparently legitimate money.

entries.name: Fan-out
entries.description: One account sends money to many different accounts in a short time, splitting a sum into smaller transfers.
red_flags: Many outgoing transfers to new counterparties in a short period
Outgoing amounts similar in size
Little incoming activity apart from one large credit
review_actions: Review the source of the large credit before the split
Check whether the recipients are linked to each other or to known cases
Request evidence from the recipients' banks for the same time window

entries.name: Fan-in
entries.description: Many different accounts send money to one account in a short time, consolidating funds.
red_flags: Many incoming transfers from new counterparties in a short period
Incoming amounts just below reporting or review thresholds
Funds leave soon after they are consolidated
review_actions: Identify the senders and whether they share attributes
Check where the consolidated funds go next
Request evidence from the senders' banks for the same time window

entries.name: Gather-scatter
entries.description: Funds are gathered from many accounts into one account, then scattered from it to many other accounts.
red_flags: High numbers of both senders and recipients for one account
Money passes through quickly with little balance left
Senders and recipients differ
review_actions: Treat the central account as a possible collection point
Map both the sending and the receiving side
Request evidence from banks on both sides

entries.name: Scatter-gather
entries.description: One account scatters money to several intermediate accounts, which each forward it to the same destination account.
red_flags: Several accounts each receive from one source and pay one destination
Intermediate accounts hold funds only briefly
Source and destination transfers close in time
review_actions: Link the intermediate accounts as one case
Check whether source and destination are related
Request evidence on the intermediates held at other banks

entries.name: Cycle
entries.description: Money moves along a chain of accounts and returns to the account it started from.
red_flags: Funds return to the originating account after several hops
Each account in the chain passes on most of what it receives
Transfers follow each other closely in time
review_actions: Reconstruct the full chain across banks
Check for common ownership among chain accounts
Request evidence from the banks holding the other chain accounts

entries.name: Random walk
entries.description: Money moves along an irregular path of transfers between accounts without a clear shape.
red_flags: Accounts pass on most of what they receive
Short holding times
Transfers between otherwise unrelated accounts
review_actions: Follow the funds forward and backward across banks
Check holding times and pass-through ratios
Request evidence on the next and previous hops

entries.name: Bipartite
entries.description: A group of source accounts sends money to a group of destination accounts, with many links between the two groups.
red_flags: Several senders pay several of the same recipients
Senders and recipients form two distinct groups
Transfers concentrated in a short period
review_actions: Map both groups and the links between them
Check whether the groups share attributes
Request evidence from banks holding members of either group

entries.name: Stack
entries.description: Several bipartite layers are stacked: money moves from one group of accounts to a second group, then to a third, and so on.
red_flags: Several layers of intermediary accounts
Each layer passes funds on quickly
Activity spread over many banks
review_actions: Reconstruct the layers across banks
Prioritise the first and last layers
Request evidence from every bank holding a layer
